findings.title: Accidental pre-change duplicate of CoreServiceFactory.test.ts committed as `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E`
findings.description: The new file `packages/core/tests/services/CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E` is a verbatim copy of the *pre-change* `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts` — its git blob hash (`e6539010`) is exactly the "before" hash in the diff header for the real file, and it still calls `createContextPipeline(FIXTURE_PROJECT_PATH)` with the old one-argument signature. It is inert (vitest's `tests/**/*.{test,spec}.{js,mjs,cjs,ts,mts,cts}` glob and `tsconfig.test.json`'s `tests/**/*` include both ignore the `.ts-E` extension), so it won't run or compile — but it is 146 lines of dead, now-stale code in the repo that will mislead anyone reading the "current" factory API. Delete it with `git rm` before merging.

findings.title: Adoption resolver decision logic and error semantics are correct
findings.description: Verified against `adoptionOutcome.ts`, `adoptionState.ts`, `sourceVolume.ts`, and `SystemPromptParser.getPromptForInstruction`: the lazy fact-reading order (state → artifacts → source volume) matches `decideOutcome`'s contract, the `never`-default in `isSelected` keeps the switch exhaustive, `persistInProgress` wraps write failures in `AdoptionError` with `cause` and a remedy, `assertGuideSupportsAdoption` runs before any write (test 12 and the resolver guide-check tests confirm state stays unset on rejection), and `ContextIntegrator.generateContextFromProject` rethrows `AdoptionError` while preserving the error-stub path for unrelated failures (both covered by new unit tests in `ContextIntegrator.test.ts`). The `brownfield-adoption` instruction constant is referenced everywhere rather than re-spelled.

findings.title: Test suite follows the testing standards
findings.description: The new tests live in the centralized `tests/` directories, use `mkdtemp` throwaway dirs with `rm` in `afterEach`, save/restore `CONTEXT_FORGE_DATA_DIR` (a dedicated test variable, never a production URL), mock `sourceVolume` at the boundary only to assert the walk is *skipped*, use behavior-oriented names, and include the production-shaped fixture (real `prompt.ai-project.system.md` with `##### Brownfield Adoption` and the `brownfield-adoption` profile) so parsers are exercised on the format they consume in production. The parity test exercises the real MCP client end-to-end. The `chmod`-based read-only write test is appropriately `skipIf` on win32/root rather than flaky.

findings.title: ContextIntegrator constructor is now 7 positional parameters
findings.description: The TypeScript rules prefer named (object) parameters for functions taking 3+ arguments. This pre-existing constructor already took six positional resolvers, and the new `resolveAdoptionFn` extends the established pattern consistently (all call sites — `CoreServiceFactory` and tests — pass positional `null`s). No action required now; if another resolver is added, consider an options object.
